newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-EX-RUSSIA COACH SAYS HE WILL JOIN CSKA MOSCOW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EX-RUSSIA COACH SAYS HE WILL JOIN CSKA MOSCOW.

text.p: Former Russian national coach Pavel Sadyrin said on Wednesday he was taking over at premier league CSKA Moscow but the club's current trainer said he was staying put, Itar-Tass news agency said.
Sadyrin told Tass he had been approached by CSKA on Monday and would take over as coach on Saturday, although he had not yet signed a contract.
Alexander Tarkhanov, who guided CSKA to fifth place in last year's championship, told Tass he knew nothing of the deal and that he was not planning to resign.
Club officials were not immediately available to comment.
Sadyrin, 54, would not face his first major challenge on the pitch until the spring, when the 1997 season begins.
Sadyrin parted company with Zenit St Petersburg last November after they finished 10th in the championship, one year after he led them back into the top league.
A 2-1 home defeat by Spartak Moscow in the last match of the season thwarted ambitions to finish in the top eight and secure a big cash bonus for the club promised by the city council.

Sadyrin had two spells as Zenit's coach and was formerly a player there. He led the club to the Soviet league title in 1984, when it was called Zenit Leningrad, but quit shortly afterwards following disputes with players.
He has also coached CSKA before and crowned his first stay by winning the last Soviet championship in 1991.

Sadyrin later became Russia's national coach but was sacked after a stormy two years which ended when Russia were knocked out of the 1994 World Cup finals. Several key players had boycotted the team, accusing the trainer of arrogance and inexperience.
